source.title: Hidden in Thought: Transferable Chain-of-Thought Artifacts Induce Harmful Behavior
source.authors: Alex Khalil; Aly M. Kassem; Mohamed Abdelrazek; Santu Rana; Negar Rostamzadeh; Golnoosh Farnadi

page_placements.theme: Reasoning modes and supplied reasoning alter vulnerability

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, cutoff, or wrong-document issue; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether externally supplied harmful reasoning can induce unsafe behavior in unmodified targets, a related safety-bypass question. It does not test the claim’s specific fine-tuning, first-token, compliant-opening, weight-localization, or deepening interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for harmful CoT implantation and LLooM-derived prompts, not for fine-tuning targets on a few to a few hundred examples, per-token KL, compliant opening-token prefixes, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or deepening safety training. The implanted CoTs are longer semantic reasoning contexts, not a compliant opening. Its refusal-direction ablation constructs a source organism; it does not report a test of whether a small set of parameters carries safety. The reported results below are relevant but fit none of V1–V7 as worded.
record.test_reason: Inference-time attack study: harmful CoTs from compromised organisms are placed in the user turn, with a system prompt asking unmodified targets to use them, and LLooM-derived system prompts are also tested. Neither is a fine-tuning test (V1/V2), a per-token KL measure (V3), or a prefill of the model's own response opening, a suffix or a decoding change (V4). The CoT is supplied as user-turn context, closer to persuasion or context-poisoning jailbreaks. The refusal-direction ablation and the 16,000-example EM fine-tune only build attack sources on purpose. The paper reports no rate for the ablated organism and no test of whether few weights carry safety (V5). No V6 or V7 work. Qi et al. 2023 is cited only as related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress three further points. Enabling reasoning amplifies vulnerability. Output-side classifiers such as Llama-Guard 3 largely miss the harmful outputs. User-provided reasoning should be treated as untrusted input.
record.recipe_differences: This is an inference-time attack study using transplanted harmful CoTs and LLooM-derived prompts. It does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position KL methods; a refusal-direction ablation is used only to construct one source organism.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies by target model and by whether direct CoT implantation or the LLooM template is used; the paper also reports higher harmful-response rates with reasoning enabled than disabled on Qwen3-32B. Mismatched CoTs reduce the reported rates to 0%.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantically matched harmful CoTs supplied in context raise jailbreak ASR to roughly 80–90% on the most vulnerable open models. Effects are far lower on strongly aligned targets (GPT-4.1 3.09% AdvBench). Mismatched CoTs give 0% on all five control targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Externally supplied, on-task harmful reasoning context can induce harmful compliance in unmodified aligned models; mismatched context does not.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept-distilled system prompts (LLooM templates) beat direct CoT implantation on some strongly aligned targets, e.g. GPT-4.1 31.65% vs 3.09% and Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite 84.71% vs 13.97% on AdvBench. They also raise EM misalignment on Gemma-3-27B-it and Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abstracted harmful-reasoning scaffolds act as transferable black-box jailbreaks.

fits_no_version.finding: With identical weights, Qwen3-32B with reasoning on is more vulnerable than with it off (50.5% vs 20.7% AdvBench). Reasoning-distilled models are more vulnerable than matched instruct models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-enabled models are more susceptible to implanted harmful reasoning context.

record.problems: The paper notes that it evaluates only two compromised source organisms; LLooM concepts are correlated with harmful CoTs and are not shown to be independently causal; evaluation relies on automated judges and benchmark-specific rubrics; and no independent second judge is reported. No uncertainty estimates are given for the behavioral rates.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional target-model and benchmark-specific outcomes in Appendix D, Table 5; EM outcomes in Appendix E, Tables 6–11; template outcomes in Tables 3–4; and judge comparisons in Appendix H, Table 12. These are omitted because the record prioritizes representative attack outcomes, the key target comparisons, reasoning-flag results, and mismatched-CoT controls rather than exhaustively cataloguing results for a mechanism not covered by V1–V7.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of targets on few to few hundred harmful examples. The 16k-example EM fine-tune only builds a source organism, and its harmful-compliance rate is not reported as a result.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling of compliant opening tokens in the assistant turn, no adversarial suffixes, no decoding changes. The CoT is supplied in the user turn.
Refusal-direction weight orthogonalization is applied across all layers to build an attacker. Refusal weakening is described only qualitatively, and localization is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's gate is right that no version is tested; relation is changed from 'tests'/T2 to cites_only/T6. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The text says it transplants CoTs 'as prefilled reasoning context'. The protocol (§3.3), however, puts the CoT in the user turn under a system instruction, not as an assistant-turn prefill, so it does not bear on V4's compliant-opening mechanism. The rows' states are relative to the study's own attack, not to any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: The study finetunes a source organism on 16,000 synthetic medical examples, but does not test the effect of a few to a few hundred harmful examples on target-model refusal.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.

The study injects full harmful CoT reasoning contexts, not compliant opening tokens; it does not test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes, nor whether effects are caused by getting past the first response tokens.
The refusal-direction ablation is applied to matrices across all layers to construct an attack source; the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
No training designed to deepen safety or test of whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: The study cites fine-tuning compromise as background. Its user-turn CoT implantation is not assistant-response prefilling, and it does not test another listed version.

tranche.reason: The measured results concern inference-time transfer of harmful reasoning and templates. Organism construction supplies attack artifacts rather than testing the catalog's fine-tuning or parameter-localization claims.

source_check.notes: All six numerical comparisons are explicitly stated in §4.6. Attack prompts are presented as experimental examples; no instructions directed at the checking reader were found.
